title: Russia is back in the hockey world championships after sports court ruling
summary: Russia teams must be allowed to play International Ice Hockey Federation events such as the world championships, the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled on Friday.

image.caption: In this May 2021 file photo, Russian men's hockey team players react during an IIHF men's hockey world championships match. A ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport on Friday has overturned an IIHF ban on Russian teams from its world championships instituted since the invasion of Ukraine in 20

blocks.text: Russia teams must be allowed to play International Ice Hockey Federation events such as the world championships, the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled on Friday.
Russia had been banned from competitions since 2022 following invasion of Ukraine
CAS overturned IIHF decisions which excluded Russia from events in the 2026-27 season including the men's and women's world championships.
In a brief statement, CAS cited a lack of sufficient evidence to support the IIHF's security concerns.

CAS said its ruling did not address issues such as whether Russia should be required to play without national symbols as a team of neutral athletes, as in some other Olympic sports, or other "organizational consequences."

items: IIHF to decide Russian hockey participation on event-by-event basis after ban review
Russia, Belarus remain banned from hockey tournaments until at least May 2026

blocks.text: The IIHF expressed disappointment with the ruling and said it "maintains that its decisions were necessary to protect the safety and security of all participants and safeguard the integrity of its competitions."
"While the IIHF respects the authority of CAS and will act in accordance with its ruling, the outcome does not remove the concerns that informed its assessments."
Russian Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyaryov wrote on the Telegram social media app that CAS "recognized the demands of the Russian Hockey Federation on key points as justified."
The IIHF has barred Russian teams from its world championships since the invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Russia also missed the Olympic hockey tournaments this year.
The ruling is an immediate challenge for new IIHF President Franz Reindl, whose home country of Germany hosts the men's world championship next year.
